topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This section introduces the lecturer, the scope of the cancer lecture series, and the learning objectives regarding cancer causation.

topics.label: Cancer Etiology: Endogenous Factors, Heredity, and Environmental Exposure
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the conceptual basis of cancer as a multi-factorial disease driven by intrinsic cellular processes, genetic predispositions, and environmental exposures supported by global epidemiological data.

topics.label: Infectious Pathogens and Viral Carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how biological agents, particularly oncogenic viruses and chronic infections, contribute to malignancy, illustrated by the mechanism of Burkitt lymphoma.

topics.label: Mechanisms of Chemical and Radiation-Induced DNA Damage
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail how physical radiation and various chemical agents, directly or via xenobiotic metabolic activation, form DNA adducts and mutations.

topics.label: Tumor Promotion, Inflammation, and Host Susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics address non-mutagenic drivers of cancer, focusing on chronic inflammation, the distinction between initiators and promoters, and the influence of host developmental stages.

topics.label: Methodologies for Investigating and Proving Carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the genomic, epidemiological, in vivo, and in vitro approaches used to identify carcinogens and assess their mutagenic capacity.

topics.label: Lecture Conclusion and Risk-Benefit Perspective
topics.groupedBecause: This section concludes the lecture by summarising the everyday balance of environmental cancer risks against practical benefits.
